# Rules

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-rule-docs.mjs from the plugin's RULE_DOCS.
     Edit packages/figma-plugin/src/rule-docs.ts and regenerate. -->

Every check Design CI runs, and how each finding is treated by default.
Severity is policy, not rule logic: set any rule to `off`, `info`, `warn`
or `error` in [`designci.config.json`](./configuration.md#rules) and every
surface — CLI, Action, Figma plugin — follows it.

## Token rules

These compare sources — the Figma snapshot against your code tokens — and run
everywhere: `designci check`, the GitHub Action, and the plugin.

### `token-value-mismatch`

**Token value mismatch** · default severity: `error`

> Mapped tokens must resolve to the same value in design and code.

**Why it matters.** A mapped pair is one design decision written down twice. When the values disagree, one side shipped something the other did not decide.

**How to fix it.** Change whichever side is wrong to match the decision, or update the decision in both places.

### `missing-token`

**Missing token** · default severity: `warn`

> Every design token should map to a token in each code source.

**Why it matters.** A token that exists only in design gets hardcoded in code — and hardcoded values drift silently.

**How to fix it.** Define the token in the code source, then map it in designci.config.json.

### `duplicate-token`

**Duplicate token** · default severity: `warn`

> A source should not define the same value under two token names.

**Why it matters.** Two names for one value fork the moment either is edited. Six months later they are two decisions nobody made.

**How to fix it.** Alias one token to the other, or delete the redundant one.

## Canvas rules

These lint the current page inside the Figma plugin: they judge **binding
state and value equality only** — never name similarity. Canvas findings are a
designer's pre-flight and deliberately never enter the health score, which
belongs to the token comparison CI runs.

### `canvas-raw-color`

**Raw color** · default severity: `warn`

> Visible fills and strokes should use a color variable or paint style, not a raw value.

**Why it matters.** Raw colors do not follow the system when it changes, and they are invisible to token comparison in CI.

**How to fix it.** Bind the fill to a color variable. When the value matches an existing token, the issue names it.

### `canvas-raw-spacing`

**Off-system spacing** · default severity: `warn`

> Auto-layout gaps and padding should come from the spacing scale.

**Why it matters.** Arbitrary spacing values erode the rhythm of the system one layout at a time.

**How to fix it.** Use a value from the space scale, or bind the field to a space variable. If the scale genuinely needs a new step, add the token first.

### `canvas-raw-radius`

**Off-system radius** · default severity: `warn`

> Corner radii should come from the radius scale.

**Why it matters.** Mixed radii across surfaces read as sloppiness even when nobody can name why.

**How to fix it.** Use a value from the radius scale, or bind the corners to a radius variable.

### `canvas-detached-instance`

**Detached instance** · default severity: `warn`

> Detached component instances should be reattached or intentionally promoted.

**Why it matters.** A detached copy no longer receives component updates — it is a fork of the component frozen at the moment of detachment.

**How to fix it.** Replace it with a fresh instance of the component, or if the divergence is intentional, make it a new component.

### `canvas-text-contrast`

**Text contrast** · default severity: `error`

> Text must meet WCAG AA contrast against its background: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text.

**Why it matters.** Low-contrast text excludes low-vision readers and fails accessibility audits after shipping, when fixes are expensive.

**How to fix it.** Darken the text or lighten the background until the ratio in the issue meets the threshold. The check only fires when both colors are confidently solid.
